title: Father! There Is No Change to Live with Thee
description: Father! There Is No Change to Live with Thee in Tonic Solfa to SONG TWENTY-TWO, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Jones Very wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 77, “God's Fatherly Care”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Tens (10.10.10.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SONG TWENTY-TWO; any other Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther! there is no change to live with Thee; Save that in Christ I grow from day to day; In each new word I hear, each thing I see, I but re-joic-ing has-ten on my way.

lines: Father! there is no change to live with Thee;
Save that in Christ I grow from day to day;
In each new word I hear, each thing I see,
I but rejoicing hasten on my way.
The morning comes, with blushes overspread,
And I, new-wakened, find a morn within;
And in its modest dawn around me shed,
Thou hear'st the prayer and the ascending hymn.
Hour follows hour, the lengthening shades descend;
Yet they could never reach as far as me.
Did not Thy love its kind protection lend,
That I, Thy child, might sleep in peace with Thee.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Jones Very died in 1880.
credits: Words by Jones Very (1813–1880), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SONG TWENTY-TWO by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
